correct_value: The screening found {{n_small}} randomized experiments below the 50-participant threshold, including c614, which randomized 48 people but does not separately report how many people contributed to the idea-score analyses.
evidence: The assembled report line 52 says "27 randomized experiments with 9 to 48 people analyzed". In forms/c614.json, studies[1] (S2) has participants.n_randomized=48 and participants.n_analyzed=null; both arms also have n_analyzed=null. forms/checks/c614.json corrections[0] instructs this distinction. I opened C:/Dropbox/Research/ai-lab/literature/creativity/Wang et al (2025) - Enhancing designer creativity through humanAI co-ideation.pdf with PyMuPDF: PDF p. 8, Participants and Design study, reports 48 recruited participants divided randomly among six groups, and Table 2 allocates eight to each group. PDF pp. 9-10 describe idea-rating analyses and idea totals without a separate analyzed-person denominator; pp. 13-14 identify Figures 11-12 as post-task survey responses. Thus the allocation count does not establish 48 people analyzed for the scored outcomes. build_report.py:119 substitutes n_randomized when n_analyzed is null; report-data.json.small_n.c614 is consequently "48", and assemble_report.py:89,105-106 uses that mixed count range in the prose template. The form already preserves the distinction. Recounting the randomized studies in the 27 small-status papers gives 47 as the largest non-null n_analyzed form value, from c134.
